olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $P,Q,R$ on sides $BC,CA,AB$ of $\triangle ABC$. $\omega_A,\omega_B,\omega_C$ = circumcircles of $\triangle AQR,\triangle BRP,\triangle CPQ$. $AP$ meets these again at $X,Y,Z$. Prove $YX/XZ=BP/PC$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n\geq 4$ equally spaced points on a circle, one labeled $A$. A marker at $A$ moves clockwise 1 or 2 steps at a time. Let $a_n$ = number of ways to go around exactly twice, starting and ending at $A$, without repeating a move. Prove $a_{n-1}+a_n=2^n$ for $n\geq 4$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n(n+1)/2$ marks in an equilateral triangle (largest row has $n$), each black-side or white-side up, initially all black. An operation: flip all marks on a line parallel to a side. Find the maximum of $f(C)$ over all achievable configurations $C$, where $f(C)$ is the minimum operations needed.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Given positive integers $m,n$, prove there is a positive integer $c$ such that $cm$ and $cn$ have the same number of occurrences of each nonzero digit in base 10.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2013

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$; find all $P$ on $BC$ such that if $X,Y$ are intersections of line $PA$ with common external tangents of circumcircles of $\triangle PAB$ and $\triangle PAC$, then $\left(\frac{PA}{XY}\right)^2+\frac{PB\cdot PC}{AB\cdot AC}=1$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2013
